variants.name: FastAPI dependency layer + Pydantic model validation
variants.idiom_name: FastAPI Depends() on the router + Pydantic models
variants.implementation_notes: FastAPI realizes the layer with dependencies: a callable declared once (`APIRouter(dependencies=[...])`) runs before every route of that surface, and path-operation parameters typed as Pydantic models are validated by the framework before the handler body executes, raising a 422 on failure. Pydantic models replace the classic validator classes - constraints are declarative fields plus before/wrap validators - and custom validators run only on raw input where the standard checks cannot express the rule. Keep the dependency on the router or app rather than per endpoint so new routes inherit it.
variants.code_sketch:
class Payload(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=64)
    count: int = Field(ge=0, le=100)

router = APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(enforce_size_and_encoding)])

@router.post("/items")
async def create(payload: Payload):   # FastAPI rejects invalid input first
    return payload
pitfalls: Per-endpoint validation drifts: a route without the dependency or without a typed model is unvalidated, so declare the layer on the router/app and assert coverage.
Plain validators terminate validation, and before/wrap validators see raw input and may mutate it - mutating then raising a later error leaks the mutation into union handling.
Dependencies run again for each request and per nested dependency; expensive rules need caching (lru_cache) or must be deferred to a cheap-first chain.

variants.name: Django MIDDLEWARE onion (get_response)
variants.implementation_notes: Django's middleware list is the intercepting layer: each middleware factory takes get_response and returns a callable that runs before the view; returning a response without calling get_response short-circuits the onion so the view (and everything inside the layer) never sees the request. Register the validator early in settings.MIDDLEWARE, and keep payload-shape rules in forms/serializers because the middleware itself cannot know each view's schema. The list order is the request order and the reverse for the response, so precedence is configuration, not code.
pitfalls: Order decides what the validator can see: rules that need the authenticated user or the session must be listed after AuthenticationMiddleware/SessionMiddleware.
Accessing request.POST inside middleware before the view can prevent later code from modifying upload handlers, and reading request.body requires care with streams.
A middleware returning a rejection still traverses the outer (earlier) middleware on the way out; keep the error shape stable so outer layers do not rewrite it.
